- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–4% for 7–14 days ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast > 82.5 and true < 78.5, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); apply 10–15% correction if true outcome drops below 75% of 14-day moving average.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.40 in 3-day window correlates with forecast divergence; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7×sentiment + 0.3×historical) for next 7 days.
